prompt.context: Alpha Capital is a private equity firm that is looking to buy a high-end male fashion retail chain named BNG. BNG is a private retail chain started in California 20 years ago. Alpha Capital is looking to see a 25% ROI in 3 years' time. They want us to help them decide whether to buy BNG, and to assess BNG's economic growth in 3 years.
prompt.question: Should Alpha Capital buy BNG, and what is Alpha Capital's assessment of BNG's economic growth in 3 years?

clarifying_info.q: How many stores does BNG have, and what is its current revenue?
clarifying_info.a: BNG has 10 retail outlets, all in California, and its annual revenue is $60 million.

clarifying_info.q: What products does BNG sell and through what channels?
clarifying_info.a: BNG sells men's jeans, shirts, and shoes, all sold only in their own boutiques to control the high-end image.
All clothing is manufactured in the U.S.

clarifying_info.q: What is the deal structure for the acquisition?
clarifying_info.a: The owner will sell the chain for a one-time payment.

clarifying_info.q: What is BNG's current profit margin?
clarifying_info.a: The chain currently experiences 20% profit margin.

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected revenue growth rate?
clarifying_info.a: Growth will be 10% for the next 3 years.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a discount rate or cost of capital to apply?
clarifying_info.a: Assume no cost of capital for this analysis.

exhibits.title: Price Sensitivity Graphs
exhibits.shows: Price sensitivity (demand) curves for two product categories: (1) belts/shoes and (2) shirts/pants, showing how volume demanded changes as price changes
exhibits.data: Indexed price on x-axis and indexed volume on y-axis. Belts/shoes curve has two kinks. Reference point: price=1, volume=1 for both categories.

framework: Macroeconomic conditions and industry growth rate
Competitive landscape and BNG's market positioning
Consumer demographics and target market potential
Sales channels and geographic expansion opportunities
Product mix and brand extension potential
Management team quality and incentive structure
Financial analysis: valuation, ROI, and growth projection

questions.prompt: What factors would you look at to assess BNG's prospects for growth?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers three buckets: (1) Macroeconomic/external factors — macro conditions, industry size and growth, competitive landscape; (2) Positioning — consumer demographics and target market size, pricing optimization potential, new sales channels (e.g., online, new geographies), product line expansion, brand awareness outside California; (3) Operations/Organization — management team quality and incentives, operational efficiency and potential to outsource manufacturing.

questions.prompt: The owner of BNG is willing to sell for a one-time payment. The chain currently has 20% profit margin and will earn $60 million next year. What factors should Alpha Capital consider to determine the maximum price to pay?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that the maximum price is a function of total expected future profits discounted at the required ROI (25%). Key factor to identify: expected revenue growth rate. Candidate should ask the interviewer for the growth rate. Strong answer explicitly frames it as: Max Price = Total Profits / (1 + Required ROI) or similar NPV/payback reasoning.

questions.prompt: Calculate the maximum amount Alpha Capital would be willing to pay for BNG.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a 3-year profit projection using 20% margin on growing revenue, then back into the purchase price that yields exactly 25% ROI on that total profit. Candidate should state the no-cost-of-capital assumption. Year 1 revenue = $60M (given as next year's figure), growing at 10% per year.

math.setup: Revenue Year 1 = $60M, profit margin = 20%, growth = 10%/yr for 3 years, required ROI = 25%, no cost of capital. Profit each year = Revenue * 20%. Max Price P such that Total Profit / P = 1.25, i.e., P = Total Profit / 1.25.
math.answer: Maximum price Alpha Capital would be willing to pay is approximately $31.6 million.

questions.prompt: BNG's 10 stores are experiencing dramatically different revenue. What do you think are the causes for this variability?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify two buckets: (1) Store Location factors — consumer population and local demographics, foot traffic (mall vs. stand-alone), proximity to competitors, local marketing efforts, proximity to supply chain affecting stock-outs; (2) Human Capital factors — quality and experience of store management and salespeople, incentive practices for staff. Interviewer should confirm that store size, product selection, and in-store promotions/signage are consistent across all locations and should be dismissed as causes.

questions.prompt: What are some of the drivers of growth of BNG?
questions.guidance: Strong answer distinguishes external from internal drivers. External: macroeconomic conditions, competitive pressures, fashion trends. Internal: products sold (variety, quality), sales channel selection (store locations), marketing effectiveness, operational efficiencies (production costs, distribution methods).

questions.prompt: Exhibit B shows price sensitivity graphs for (1) belts/shoes and (2) shirts/pants. What are your immediate reactions, and what can BNG do to increase profits? Also, what do the two kinks in the belts/shoes curve mean?
questions.guidance: (a) Candidate should identify that BNG is in the inelastic portion of the demand curve for belts/shoes and the elastic portion for shirts/pants. For belts/shoes: raising price increases total revenue — e.g., price from 1.0 to 1.2 drops volume from 1.0 to 0.9, revenue goes from 1.0 to 1.08, a net 8% revenue increase with lower variable costs (fewer units sold), improving profit. For shirts/pants: lowering price increases volume — e.g., price from 1.0 to 0.8 raises volume from 1.0 to 1.8, revenue goes from 1.0 to 1.44; but whether this improves profitability depends on the cost structure (variable costs), so candidate should caveat accordingly. (b) The two kinks represent competitors' price points — likely a competitor with both a high-end and a low-end line of belts/shoes.

math.setup: Indexed price-volume analysis for belts/shoes and shirts/pants.
steps: Belts/shoes: current revenue index = 1.0 * 1.0 = 1.0; raise price to 1.2, volume falls to 0.9; new revenue = 1.2 * 0.9 = 1.08 (+8%); profit improves by >8% due to lower variable costs.
Shirts/pants: lower price to 0.8, volume rises to 1.8; new revenue = 0.8 * 1.8 = 1.44 (+44%); profitability impact unclear without cost structure data.
math.answer: Raise belts/shoes price to boost profit by at least 8%. Lowering shirts/pants price increases revenue 44% but needs cost data to confirm profit impact.

questions.prompt: BNG is considering opening 14 new stores. What factors are most important for the CEO to consider?
questions.guidance: Open-ended synthesis question. Strong answer draws from the full case: location selection (demographics, foot traffic, competitor proximity, supply chain proximity), human capital (hiring and incentivizing quality store management), financials (capital required vs. projected revenue/profit from new stores and consistency with 25% ROI target), operational readiness (supply chain capacity for more stores, brand consistency), and market expansion considerations (geographic diversification beyond California, brand awareness building).

brainstorming.prompt: What factors are most important for BNG's CEO to consider when opening 14 new stores?

categories.name: Location Selection
ideas: Consumer demographics and consistency with high-end male target market
Proximity to existing or new competitors

categories.name: Supply Chain and Operations
ideas: Proximity to supply chain to avoid stock-outs

categories.name: Human Capital
ideas: Quality of store managers in new locations
Training programs to maintain brand standards

categories.name: Financial Viability
ideas: Capital required for build-out and inventory
Projected revenue and profit margin per new store
Consistency of new store returns with 25% ROI target

categories.name: Brand and Market Strategy
ideas: Brand awareness in new markets outside California
Maintaining high-end brand image at scale

recommendation: Alpha Capital should proceed with the acquisition of BNG if the purchase price does not exceed approximately $31.6 million, which is the maximum price that delivers the required 25% ROI over 3 years based on projected profits of $39.5 million.
BNG shows strong fundamentals: an established high-end brand with controlled distribution, 20% profit margin, and projected 10% annual revenue growth.
risks: Revenue growth of 10% is an assumption that could be undermined by macroeconomic headwinds, fashion trend shifts, or intensifying competition.
Significant revenue variability across the 10 existing stores suggests operational and location-quality inconsistencies that may be amplified when scaling to 14 new stores.
All-U.S. manufacturing and California concentration create supply chain and geographic concentration risks.
Assuming no cost of capital understates the true required return; if a discount rate is applied, the maximum justifiable purchase price falls below $31.6 million.
next_steps: Conduct due diligence on the root causes of cross-store revenue variability and assess whether underperforming stores can be improved or closed.
Analyze the price sensitivity data to implement price increases on belts/shoes immediately, locking in a quick profit improvement.
Evaluate the 14-store expansion plan with rigorous location scoring criteria before committing capital.
Model scenarios with a cost of capital to stress-test the $31.6M valuation.
